title: Anticipatory decode pipeline: kernel selection, scheduler hooks, and KV onboarding (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope

This note sketches an "anticipatory" decode pipeline that combines: (1) early kernel selection based on coarse request metadata, (2) scheduler hooks to allow low-latency prefetching / kernel warmups, and (3) KV-cache onboarding rules for new model variants. The goal is a pragmatic rollout/onboarding checklist + metrics/rollback criteria that are operationally actionable during model integration or when enabling faster decode paths (e.g., fp16-quantized kernels, fused-attention variants, lookahead batches).

Why this exists (context)

We keep seeing two classes of failures when we flip on optimized kernels or speculative batching:
- Quiet throughput regressions under tail loads: average tokens/s looks fine but p95/p99 latency spikes or per-tenant QoS degrades.
- Cold-start / cache-mismatch problems: KV cache warming or kernel-specific memory layouts produce OOMs or incorrect key eviction behavior with longer sequences.

This doc attempts to unify the acceptance criteria and operational hooks so that engineers can safely turn on anticipatory behaviors while minimizing customer impact.

High-level design

1) Early kernel selection pass
- On request arrival we run a cheap classifier that examines: model_id, requested max_tokens, user-tier, routing policy, sequence_length_hint (if provided), and any explicit flags (e.g., prefer-quantized).
- Output: kernel_profile_id (e.g., "kern-v1-fusedattn-fp16", "kern-v1-matmul-int8-legacy"), expected_memory_window, kv_compatibility_flags.
- Constraints: must be <500 microseconds added to head-of-line. Implemented as a table-driven decision function with optional learned weights (future).

2) Scheduler hooks and anticipatory actions
- scheduler.on_assign(route, kernel_profile_id): invoked when a request is placed on a GPU queue. Hooks can trigger:
  - kernel warmup: enqueue a 1-token warmup using the chosen kernel on an otherwise idle worker (cheap compile path).
  - KV prefetch: if sequence_length_hint > threshold and KV cache is cold for model+tenant, request a prefix fetch from NVRAM or promote from shared cache.
  - affinity tagging: mark the work item so routing keeps subsequent requests to same model/tenant on same GPU if possible (reduces KV churn).
- time budgets: any anticipatory action must be bounded (e.g., kernel warmup < 8ms on prod GPUs).

3) KV-cache onboarding and compatibility rules
- Onboarding metadata for model variants must include: cache_format_version, kv_prefetch_granularity, tolerance_policy (strict | best-effort), and eviction_hint.
- If kernel_profile_id changes cache_format_version incompatibly, onboarding must fail fast or run in a canary mode where both cache formats are maintained for a small traffic slice.
- Provide a migration path: when format change needed, we maintain read-through compatibility layer that returns data in the newer shape until we can rehydrate.

Model integration checklist (acceptance)

Minimum acceptance criteria before full rollout of kernel_profile or anticipatory behaviors:
- Unit tests: kernel execution correctness on short sequences and typical prompt patterns (smoke + edge token ids).
- Integration tests: single-GPU with KV cache enabled; must pass a suite including: long-context (> 8k tokens) generation, multiple streams converging on same KV keys, and tenant isolation tests.
- Perf baselines: comparisons to baseline kernel (current default) using representative workloads (3 traffic patterns: chat, summarization, long-form doc). Required: median token latency improvement OR cost reduction >= 5% without p99 latency regression > 10% absolute or relative (configurable).
- Stability window: run canary for at least 72 hours at 1–3% traffic, capturing readiness signals below.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts provisioned (see metrics below).

Suggested automated gating pipeline (CI/CD)
- CI-run: microbench + fuzz for potential memory footprints.
- Pre-prod run: reproduce 1-hour window of production traffic (recorded) on staging cluster, capture gradients and p99 latency.
- Canary rollout: 1% -> 3% -> 10% with automated checks at each step. Rollback if any check fails.

Rollback criteria and playbook

Automated rollback triggers (any single condition):
- p99 token latency increase > 25% and absolute increase > 50ms sustained for 5 minutes.
- Error rate (5xx or decode failures) increase > 1% absolute.
- GPU OOMs: any OOMs attributable to kernel change across >= 2 distinct hosts within 10 minutes.
- KV cache mismatch errors (format/conflict) > 0.1% of requests.

Rollback steps (playbook)
- Step 0 (detection): Alert fires, paging engineers + oncall.
- Step 1 (quarantine): Pause rollout, set canary weight to 0% via routing control.
- Step 2 (investigate): Collect traces and full kernels/params for failed requests. Attach memory profiles.
- Step 3 (mitigation): Switch affected tenants to fallback kernel_profile_id (fast path revert). If KV format is at fault, enable read-through compatibility layer.
- Step 4 (post-mortem): 72-hour RCA with timeline and hotfix plan. Re-run CI pre-prod with targeted reproducer.

Metrics and dashboards (what to monitor)

Core metrics (per model_id, per kernel_profile_id, per tenant):
- token_latency.{p50,p90,p95,p99} (ms) — token generation latencies measured end-to-end.
- request_error_rate (%) — decode failures, serialization errors, sanity-check violations.
- gpu_memory_headroom (MB) — free memory distribution across active workers.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio (per tenant) — both prefix and suffix hits.
- kv_cache_loading_time (ms) — time to load or rehydrate a prefix from cold storage.
- kernel_compile_time (ms) — time spent compiling/warming kernel on worker.
- tenant_qos_score — composite metric combining latency, errors, and token throughput scaled to tenant SLO.

Derived signals / alerts
- sudden_drop_in_kv_hit_ratio > 10% relative in 2 minutes for a tenant -> page SRE.
- kernel_compile_time spike beyond historical baseline (zscore > 4) -> investigate JIT cache churn.
- sustained p99 latency increase as noted in rollback triggers.

Operational experiments and data collection

We should collect additional fields during the canary:
- sequence_length_hint (if provided by client) and actual sequence_lengths observed.
- cache_format_version per request (for correlation).
- kernel_profile_id chosen and whether fallback was used.
- scheduler decisions: affinity assigned, warmup triggered, prefetch executed, time spent in each hook.

Safety nets and conservative defaults

- Default behavior: if early kernel selection observes uncertainty (low confidence or incompatible flags), choose the conservative kernel (baseline) and skip anticipatory actions.
- Warmup throttling: limit warmups to X per host per second (configurable; default 2/sec) to avoid noisy background work.
- Prefetch budget: set bytes/sec and concurrent prefetch limits per tenant to preserve I/O headroom.

Onboarding example (concrete flow)

1) Model variant uploaded: includes metadata file with kernel hints, cache_format_version=2.
2) Integration tests run in staging.
3) CI posts results to the canary dashboard.
4) Canary starts at 1% traffic with kernel_profile_id=v2-warmfast.
5) Scheduler hooks warm kernel on idle workers and prefetch prefixes for long prompts.
6) After 72 hours and checks pass, rollout to 10% then 50% then 100%.

Open questions / TODOs

- Confidence scoring for kernel selection: how do we measure "confidence" cheaply? ML-based selector vs heuristics table? (Rohan to prototype ML selector in INF-2147)
- Compatibility matrix for KV formats: need a small DSL to describe compatibility and automated transformer for read-through adapters. Who owns? (Marta)
- Affinity policy tradeoffs: how aggressive should affinity be for multi-tenant hosts? We must balance KV warm caches vs hotspotting. Proposal: soft-affinity with decay after N requests.
- Dashboard templates: SRE/Observability to create a standard dashboard with per-canary views and a single-click revert button. (Liu to draft)

Appendix: quick checklist for oncall when a canary trips

- Capture a sample trace for 500 affected requests.
- Identify top 5 failing endpoints and their kernel_profile_id.
- Check GPU memory profiles across hosts and presence of OOMs.
- Confirm KV format mismatch by sampling headers.
- If revert safe: flip canary to baseline and monitor for 2x p99 windows.

Notes to self / rough notes

- Keep anticipatory work as opt-in feature flag per model variant.
- Consider adding a fallback layer that can synthesize short prefixes for warmup when KV cold.
- We should protect free-tier tenants from aggressive prefetching by default to minimize cost.

References and related docs

- See INF-2147 for early experiments on lookahead decode classifier.
- See PR #402 for kernel compile caching improvements.
- Related: lookahead-decoding notes (older) — avoid reusing identical text to keep this doc fresh.

----

This doc is intentionally lightweight and practical: the goal is to give the SRE and serving-runtime teams a single checklist and a set of deterministic rollback criteria so we can enable more aggressive decode optimizations without surprises. Please add examples, reproducer scripts, and a staging dashboard template as follow-ups.
